title: Voidable marriages: who may file, when, and ratification

rows.h: (1) No parental consent, party 18 to below 21
c: The party whose parent or guardian did not give consent; or the parent, guardian or person having legal charge of the party
Party: within five years after attaining 21. Parent or guardian: at any time before the party reaches 21
Yes: if the party freely cohabited with the other after attaining 21

rows.h: (2) Either party of unsound mind
c: The sane spouse who had no knowledge of the other's insanity; any relative, guardian or person having legal charge of the insane; or the insane spouse during a lucid interval or after regaining sanity
At any time before the death of either party
Yes: if the insane party, after coming to reason, freely cohabited with the other

rows.h: (3) Consent obtained by fraud (Art. 46)
c: Within five years after the discovery of the fraud
Yes: if the injured party, with full knowledge of the facts constituting the fraud, freely cohabited with the other

rows.h: (4) Consent obtained by force, intimidation or undue influence
c: Within five years from the time the force, intimidation or undue influence disappeared or ceased
Yes: if, after the force, intimidation or undue influence disappeared or ceased, the injured party freely cohabited with the other

rows.h: (5) Physical incapacity to consummate, continuing and appearing incurable
c: Within five years after the celebration of the marriage
No: cannot be ratified by cohabitation

rows.h: (6) Sexually transmissible disease, serious and appearing incurable
c: Within five years after the celebration of the marriage
No: cannot be ratified by cohabitation

title: Void vs. voidable vs. legal separation

cols.h: Children conceived or born before the decree

rows.h: Declaration of absolute nullity (void marriage)
c: Void from the beginning, but a judicial declaration is needed before remarrying (Art. 40)
Solely the husband or the wife (A.M. No. 02-11-10-SC), for marriages governed by the Family Code
Illegitimate, except children of Art. 36 and Art. 53 marriages, who are legitimate (Art. 54)

rows.h: Annulment (voidable marriage)
c: Only the persons named in Art. 47 for each ground
The periods in Art. 47 for each ground
Severed; a party may remarry once the Art. 52 requirements are recorded
Legitimate if conceived or born before the judgment becomes final and executory (Art. 54)

rows.h: Legal separation
c: Within five years from the occurrence of the cause (Art. 57)
Not severed; the spouses are entitled to live separately (Art. 63(1))

rows.h: Incumbent member of the judiciary
Priest, rabbi, imam or minister of a church or religious sect
c: Duly authorized by his church, registered with the civil registrar general, acting within the limits of his written authority, and at least one party belongs to his church

rows.h: Ship captain or airplane chief
c: Only marriages in articulo mortis between passengers or crew members, while at sea or in flight, and also during stopovers at ports of call (Art. 31)

rows.h: Military commander of a unit to which a chaplain is assigned
c: Only marriages in articulo mortis between persons within the zone of military operation, in the absence of the chaplain (Art. 32)

rows.h: Consul-general, consul or vice-consul
c: Only marriages between Filipino citizens abroad (Art. 10)

rows.h: City or municipal mayor
c: Authority restored by the Local Government Code of 1991

title: Marriages exempt from the license requirement

rows.h: Art. 27
c: Either or both parties at the point of death; the marriage stays valid even if the ailing party survives

rows.h: Art. 28
c: The residence of either party has no means of transportation to enable them to appear personally before the local civil registrar

rows.h: Art. 31
c: In articulo mortis between passengers or crew members, solemnized by the ship captain or airplane pilot

rows.h: Art. 32
c: In articulo mortis between persons within the zone of military operation, solemnized by the military commander in the absence of the chaplain

rows.h: Art. 33
c: Among Muslims or members of ethnic cultural communities, performed according to their customs, rites or practices

rows.h: Art. 34
c: A man and a woman who have lived together as husband and wife for at least five years without any legal impediment to marry each other

rows.h: Condonation
c: The aggrieved party has forgiven the offense or act complained of, after it was committed

rows.h: Consent
c: The aggrieved party agreed in advance to the commission of the offense or act

rows.h: Connivance
c: The parties cooperated in bringing about the commission of the offense or act

rows.h: Mutual guilt (recrimination)
c: Both parties have given ground for legal separation

rows.h: Collusion
c: The parties agreed to obtain the decree of legal separation, as by fabricating a ground

rows.h: Prescription
c: The action was not filed within five years from the occurrence of the cause
